claim:
For every real \(2<p<\infty\), let \(X_p\) be the Day--James plane on \(\mathbb R^2\) with
\[
\|(x,y)\|_{X_p}=
\begin{cases}
\bigl(|x|^p+|y|^p\bigr)^{1/p},&xy\ge0,\\
\max\{|x|,|y|\},&xy\le0.
\end{cases}
\]
Then its Ptolemy constant is exactly
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(X_p)=1+2^{-2/p}.
\]
Since the published James constant of this family is \(J(X_p)=1+2^{-1/p}\), one has the exact identity
\[
C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(X_p)=1+\bigl(J(X_p)-1\bigr)^2.
\]

correctness.rationale: For tau=2^{-2/p}, H_tau^2=(x+y)^2+tau(x-y)^2 is analyzed on both exhaustive sign sectors. On xy>=0, sharp two-coordinate ell_p/ell_2 inequalities give 1+tau <= H_tau^2/N_p^2 <= 4tau. On xy<=0, the exact ratio 4(s^2+tau)/(1+s)^2 has unique minimum 4tau/(1+tau) at s=tau and maximum 4tau. Hilbert Ptolemy gives C_Pt<=1+tau. The explicit triple x=(-tau,-tau), y=(1,-1), z=x+y has ratio exactly 1+tau. No finite enumeration is used.

value.rationale: The Day--James ell_p-ell_infinity planes are a classical parameter family for exact Banach-space constants. The result determines a distinct standard four-point invariant across the entire super-Hilbert range, identifies one uniform extremal construction, and yields the exact structural identity C_Pt=1+(J-1)^2.
